reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes BitClub Network participation through bitcoin and mining-pool purchases, registration, and a recruitment-linked payment structure with cycle rewards and percentage-based bonuses. It claims participants may earn up to $2,000 per day and directs viewers to register with sponsor assistance, though the available video evidence does not establish whether the stated returns or support were delivered.

opening.argument: Judge the income figures as claims to evaluate, not proof that returns were guaranteed. The speaker explicitly says, “It is always necessary to consider the risk,” and tells viewers they can check the operation without relying on him. That matters when assessing whether this is a deceptive promise rather than a presentation of a risky investment proposal. His invitation to ask questions also leaves room for scrutiny.

You can check it all and not have to believe me. Absolutely not.
Write a question Get an answer.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited mining-firm description and binary structure establish what he discusses, not that a viewer is promised a risk-free return or that the figures were paid. The opening itself concedes the available evidence does not establish whether returns were delivered. His express risk qualification and invitation to check the claims deserve weight even alongside the purchase pitch.

citations.quote: It is always necessary to consider the risk
You can check it all and not have to believe me. Absolutely not.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A brief risk qualification does not change the offer being promoted. The speaker urges viewers to register, buy bitcoins and buy pools, while presenting substantial daily earnings as attainable. Saying viewers may check his claims does not provide evidence that the mining returns exist or offset the direct solicitation.

opening.argument: Much of this webinar works as an explanation of how the program operates. The speaker introduces a discussion of what BitClub is and how it should be used, walks through a binary structure, and discusses financial planning courses. Those details give the judge a reason to read the numerical examples as instructional material within a business presentation, rather than treating every described bonus as a promise to the viewer.

citations.quote: For this session we will discuss what is a BitClub as an instrument, how should we use it
A binary system is used for grid structure. It means that you only have to register two people in your first line
this is a financial planning school, from which wealth begins

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening quotes the binary explanation and mining-firm description, but those excerpts also fit a presentation explaining a business model. A description of cycles does not, on its own, establish that anyone received the stated reward. The speaker says the session will address how the program should be used, a purpose broader than the opening's focus on solicitation.

citations.quote: For this session we will discuss what is a BitClub as an instrument, how should we use it
The cycle is called 15 and 15, and the cycle works out, this credit is written off from your account and a reward amount in the size of $200.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The explanation is part of the pitch, not a detached tutorial. After describing courses, the speaker tells viewers to buy BitClub assets and register immediately; he specifies that registration leads to buying bitcoins and pools. The instructional format does not remove the paid mining offer at the center of the presentation.

citations.quote: Those are the things I tell you to do, investors, to buy assets in Bit Club Network. Register right now, the register button is below, at the bottom.
First steps will start with registration, of course, buying bitcoins and will end by buying pools.

opening.argument: The presentation openly describes a paid club offering: membership, pools at stated prices, courses and a referral-based bonus structure. Those features can be assessed as a commercial offer without assuming, from this video alone, that payments are fabricated or that promised support fails to arrive. The speaker identifies both purchases and reinvestments as the basis for referral percentages; he does not hide that commissions are involved. The evidence supports caution about the offer, but does not independently establish its performance.

citations.quote: Besides, being an opportunity for your customers, you also receive free access to the courses which we present as a bonus
For the activity of the these people five percent of the purchase of the pools, and ten percent from their reinvestments.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening correctly identifies pool purchases and team-linked rewards, but neither feature alone establishes that the paid offering lacked a service or that the stated rewards were not delivered. Its own acknowledgment that delivery is unestablished cuts both ways. The presentation also describes course access, which the opening leaves out when characterizing what membership offers.

citations.quote: you also receive free access to the courses which we present as a bonus

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Course access does not explain away the central paid mining proposition. The slide says pools bring income over 1,000 days, and the speaker directs viewers from registration to bitcoin and pool purchases. He also describes rewards generated by the purchases of invited people. The concern is the promoted return mechanism, not a claim that this video proves whether any individual payment was ultimately delivered.
